close_reason: Done in 1a95410. Added 'Field-type rationale' section to ClientConfig rustdoc explaining the u64-for-HTTP-body-caps vs usize-for-in-memory-frame-caps split (reqwest reports Content-Length as u64; tungstenite WebSocketConfig wants usize). Added 'No cross-field invariants' section explicitly documenting that validate() checks each field independently. Doc-only; no behavior change. The optional cross-field warning recommendation (max_sse_frame > max_call_body hint) was rejected as bikeshedding — they govern different threats (per-frame vs whole-body) and a deployment can rationally configure them in either order.
description:
client.rs:36-81 — ClientConfig struct with seven pub fields.

#[non_exhaustive] correctly allows adding fields. But:

1. Every field is pub. Callers reading config.max_call_body, mutating with .max_call_body = ..., or pattern-destructuring (let ClientConfig { max_call_body, .. } = config) are committed. The crate cannot replace u64 with a NonZeroU64 newtype later — that would be a breaking change at every caller site even though it would catch the bug Class A: 'I set max_call_body to 0 and got InvalidArgument at the constructor instead of compile-time'.

2. Two semantically-related fields (max_sse_frame, max_ws_message) are usize while three (max_session_body, max_call_body, max_download_body, max_upload_response_body) are u64. The mixed-int-type API forces callers writing `max_sse_frame: 1024 * 1024` versus `max_session_body: 1024 * 1024` — without a `_u64` suffix, the literals are different types. Callers who try to write a helper `fn limit_for(kind: BodyKind) -> impl Into<Both>` discover the mismatch. Should have been one numeric type (u64 throughout, with internal casts to usize where needed).

3. There is no constraint that max_sse_frame <= max_call_body or other cross-field invariants. A caller can configure max_sse_frame = 2 MiB but max_call_body = 1 MiB and get inconsistent behavior — a single SSE event survives, but a JSON response of the same size triggers ResponseTooLarge. validate() should at least flag if max_sse_frame > max_call_body as a hint.

Recommendation (low priority because it's a 0.x crate): document the rationale for the mixed types in the field docstrings, and consider in next minor release whether to add cross-field warnings to validate().
title: ClientConfig field set is public; future fields cannot remove existing ones without major bump
